We selected FIC-A for follow-up spectroscopy because it had previously been identified as a Galactic unbound candidate.
Our new spectrum gives a heliocentric radial velocity of 520 ± 10 km/s for FIC-A. Previous Study reported 550 ± 20 km/s in the same frame.
Our new observations and analysis lead us to conclude that FIC-A is bound to the Milky Way.
For FIC-A under Model A, the heliocentric distance has a 95% credible interval from 7 to 10 kpc; no central value is reported.
For FIC-A under Model B, the heliocentric distance is in the interval from 8 to 12 kpc; no statistical interpretation or central value is stated.
For FIC-A under Model C, the heliocentric distance is 8.0 kpc with an upper uncertainty of 0.5 kpc; a lower uncertainty is not reported.
For FIC-A under Model D, the heliocentric distance is 9.0 kpc. The authors report a total uncertainty of 0.5 kpc and named components of 0.3 kpc (statistical) and 0.4 kpc (systematic).
For FIC-A under Model Z, the reported Galactic unbound probability is 0%.
The attached JSON reports the measured parallax of FIC-A in mas.
